text:
If you’re taking a boat onto Lake Champlain today, take the Lake Wind Advisory seriously. Winds will shift from southwest to northwest and build to 15 to 20 knots, with gusts around 25 and waves up to 2 feet. On land, it’s a bright, breezy day with a high right around 76, though that wind will make the waterfront feel rougher than the temperature suggests. The forecast keeps rain to a stray shower, but the models are unusually split, with rain chances ranging from 55 to 100 percent. I’d keep a light jacket handy, though the forecasters’ own discussion sees no significant weather trouble.

Tonight turns cooler quickly, with a slight shower chance around 8 or 9, then clearing toward a low near 53. Friday looks sunny and quieter, with a high around 71 and a northwest breeze. The lake stays active tomorrow, with 10 to 15-knot winds and 1- to 2-foot waves. Good day for a shoreline walk, but I’d stay off the broad water this afternoon unless you’re comfortable with gusty conditions.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Thursday! For the most part, the rain from yesterday is gone and out of here. As expected, most places received about 0.5 to 1 inch of new rain with a few areas locally higher or slightly lower. Into the rest of our day, sunshine is emerging this afternoon, as high temperatures climb back into the mid and upper 70s. A few more clouds will roll in tonight as a cold front passes through the area. Overnight lows will fall into the 40s and lower 50s to start Friday.
